title: Everyday Worship
description: A question bank on purification, prayer, fasting, charity, supplication and remembrance, with practical scenarios and primary-text references. Focuses on broadly shared Sunni teachings; detailed school-specific rulings and individual fatwas are outside its scope.
difficultyMethod: Editorial classification; not calibrated from learner response data. Advanced means greater reasoning depth within this subject, not a scholarly qualification.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Handle I am not sure as a UI action, not as a fifth answer option.

questions.question: How many obligatory daily prayers are prescribed in the narration of Sahih al-Bukhari 46?

options.text: Five
Three
Four
Seven

questions.explanation: The narration identifies five prayers during the day and night, distinguishing them from additional voluntary prayer.

questions.question: Which voluntary daytime prayer is included as two rakahs in the advice to Abu Hurayrah in Sahih al-Bukhari 1981?

options.text: The Eid al-Fitr prayer
Duha, the forenoon prayer
The funeral prayer
The Friday congregational prayer

questions.explanation: Abu Hurayrah reports advice to pray two rakahs of Duha, alongside monthly fasting and witr before sleep.

questions.question: Which action is explicitly included in the purification instructions of Quran 5:6?

options.text: Washing only one's clothes
Perfuming the hands instead of washing
Washing the face
Washing only the hair

questions.explanation: Al-Maidah 5:6 includes washing the face among the instructions for purification before prayer.

questions.question: In Quran 5:6, what action is specified concerning the head?

options.text: Shaving it before every prayer
Covering it with perfume
Washing it exactly seven times
Wiping it

questions.explanation: The verse instructs wiping the head. This question does not ask about differences over the extent of wiping.

questions.question: What does Quran 5:6 instruct for someone in a state of janabah?

options.text: Full purification through bathing
Only changing their outer clothing
Only washing their hands
Postponing all purification for a week

questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes purification from janabah from the ordinary ablution instructions.

questions.question: What alternative purification is named in Quran 5:6 when its conditions are met and water cannot be found?

options.text: Replacing prayer with a donation
Tayammum using clean earth
Skipping purification without an alternative
Washing with perfume alone

questions.explanation: The verse prescribes tayammum rather than treating the absence of water as the end of worship.

questions.question: How does Quran 4:103 describe prayer for believers?

options.text: An act with no connection to time
A practice required only during travel
An obligation at appointed times
A duty performed only once in a lifetime

questions.explanation: An-Nisa 4:103 emphasizes prescribed prayer times.

questions.question: Toward which sacred place does Quran 2:144 direct the worshipper?

options.text: The cave of Hira
Mount Uhud
The palace of a ruler
Al-Masjid al-Haram

questions.explanation: The verse directs the Prophet and believers toward Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 631, whose practice provides the model for prayer?

options.text: The Prophet's prayer
The most popular local celebrity's preference
Any individual's invented routine
A ruler's preferred gestures

questions.explanation: The Prophet instructed the visitors to pray following the prayer they had observed him perform.

questions.question: In Sahih al-Bukhari 757, what follows bowing before the next prostration?

options.text: Moving directly to the final salutation
Rising until standing upright
Ending the prayer immediately
Beginning another prayer without rising

questions.explanation: The instruction includes bowing, returning to an upright standing position and then prostration, with composure in the postures.

questions.question: In Sahih Muslim 482, in which posture is a servant described as nearest to their Lord?

options.text: Walking to a market
Sitting at a meal
Prostration
Standing in a queue

questions.explanation: The narration associates prostration with nearness to Allah and encourages supplication in it.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 611, what is a listener instructed to do on hearing the call to prayer?

options.text: Ignore it as unrelated to worship.
Start a competing call to drown it out.
Treat it as permission to mock the caller.
Repeat what the caller says.

questions.explanation: The narration teaches attentive response to the call. Other reports explain particular response phrases.

questions.question: Which month is the obligatory fasting month identified in Quran 2:185?

options.text: Ramadan
Muharram
Rajab
Safar

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:185 connects the month of Ramadan with the instruction to fast.

questions.question: Which purpose of fasting is stated in Quran 2:183?

options.text: Guaranteeing social recognition
Developing mindfulness of Allah
Removing every need to control speech
Requiring permanent abstention from food

questions.explanation: The verse connects prescribed fasting with taqwa, or mindfulness of Allah.

questions.question: According to Quran 2:187, when does the daily fasting period begin?

options.text: At sunrise
At midday
At the onset of dawn
At sunset

questions.explanation: The verse permits eating and drinking until dawn becomes distinct, then commands completing the fast until night.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 1954, what marks the time to end the day's fast?

options.text: The following sunrise
The disappearance of all stars
Midnight in every location
Sunset, as night approaches and day withdraws

questions.explanation: The narration links the end of fasting to the setting of the sun and the arrival of night.

questions.question: What reason does Sahih al-Bukhari 1923 give for taking suhur?

options.text: There is blessing in the pre-dawn meal.
It guarantees that a person never feels hungry.
It replaces the need to fast.
It must be eaten after sunrise.

questions.explanation: The narration encourages suhur because of its blessing.

questions.question: What practice does Sahih al-Bukhari 1957 encourage once the fast's ending time has arrived?

options.text: Waiting until midnight as a daily rule
Breaking the fast without unnecessary delay
Continuing without food until the next evening
Delaying solely to appear more devout

questions.explanation: The report praises prompt breaking of the fast, not eating before its proper time.

questions.question: On which two days does Sahih al-Bukhari 1990 prohibit fasting?

options.text: Every Monday and Thursday
The first two days of every month
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
Every Friday and Saturday

questions.explanation: The narration identifies the two Eid days as days on which fasting is prohibited.

questions.question: How many days of fasting each month are included in the advice to Abu Hurayrah in Sahih al-Bukhari 1981?

options.text: One
Seven
Ten
Three

questions.explanation: The advice includes fasting three days each month, along with other acts of worship.

questions.question: Which group is explicitly included among zakat recipients in Quran 9:60?

options.text: The poor and needy
Only wealthy donors
Only the donor's business partners
Only people who promise repayment

questions.explanation: At-Tawbah 9:60 specifies recipient categories, including the poor and needy.

questions.question: What does Sahih al-Bukhari 1417 teach about giving even half a date in charity?

options.text: Only expensive gifts have value.
A small gift can still matter.
A gift counts only if photographed.
Charity must always be beyond one's means.

questions.explanation: The narration encourages charity even when the amount available is very small.

questions.question: Which everyday action is included as charity in Sahih al-Bukhari 2989?

options.text: Leaving hazards for others to manage
Mocking someone who needs help
Removing something harmful from a path
Refusing to reconcile fairly

questions.explanation: The narration includes helpful everyday actions among forms of charity.

questions.question: How does Quran 7:55 instruct people to call on their Lord?

options.text: With arrogance and demands
Only to impress an audience
By insisting that Allah is unaware of their needs
Humbly and privately

questions.explanation: Al-Araf 7:55 connects supplication with humility and discretion.

questions.question: What combination is requested in the supplication in Quran 2:201?

options.text: Good in this world, good in the Hereafter and protection from the Fire
Worldly wealth while rejecting the Hereafter
Knowledge of the date of the Hour
Public status instead of any spiritual good

questions.explanation: The supplication seeks comprehensive good rather than restricting concern to worldly life.

questions.question: Which postures for remembering Allah are named in Quran 3:191?

options.text: Only standing in a mosque
Standing, sitting and lying on one's side
Only sitting after a public speech
Only lying down before sunrise

questions.explanation: The verse describes remembrance in different everyday postures, alongside reflection on creation.

questions.question: What does Subhan Allah express?

options.text: Asking another person for payment
Announcing the start of a journey
Declaring Allah free from imperfection
Describing oneself as sinless

questions.explanation: Tasbih glorifies Allah and declares His transcendence above imperfection. The phrase appears among the forms of remembrance in the cited narration.

questions.question: What does Alhamdulillah express?

options.text: I have no need to be grateful.
Every person is beyond error.
Wealth is the only blessing.
Praise belongs to Allah.

questions.explanation: The phrase expresses praise of Allah and is included among the beloved words of remembrance in the cited report.

questions.question: What is a person doing when asking Allah to forgive them?

options.text: Seeking forgiveness
Declaring that repentance is impossible
Claiming to know every hidden matter
Making a payment to another person

questions.explanation: An-Nisa 4:110 connects wrongdoing followed by seeking Allah's forgiveness with finding Him forgiving and merciful.

questions.question: According to Aishah's report in Sahih al-Bukhari 2024, what did the Prophet do in Ramadan's last ten nights?

options.text: Stopped all night worship
Intensified worship and woke his family
Forbade his family from praying
Treated the nights as unrelated to Ramadan

questions.explanation: Aishah describes increased dedication and waking the household during the final ten nights.

questions.question: A worshipper is certain they had wudu but merely imagines that they may have passed wind. What principle is illustrated by Sahih al-Bukhari 137?

options.text: Every doubtful sensation certainly invalidates wudu.
No event can ever invalidate wudu.
Do not abandon established purity because of mere doubt.
Only the time shown on a clock decides purity.

questions.explanation: The report tells a person troubled by doubt not to leave prayer without an indication establishing the event. It distinguishes suspicion from certainty.

questions.question: A person cannot stand for prayer because of illness. What accommodation is given in Sahih al-Bukhari 1117?

options.text: Abandon all prayer until able to run.
Replace every prayer permanently with money.
Stand regardless of inability.
Pray sitting; if unable, on one's side.

questions.explanation: The instruction adapts posture to ability rather than treating inability to stand as the end of prayer.

questions.question: A person genuinely forgets a prayer and later remembers it. What does Sahih al-Bukhari 597 instruct?

options.text: Pray it when remembered.
Leave it permanently because its time passed.
Wait until the same weekday next week.
Replace it with an unrelated voluntary fast.

questions.explanation: The narration directly addresses a forgotten prayer and instructs performance when it is remembered.

questions.question: A learner rushes through bowing and prostration without settling. Which feature of Sahih al-Bukhari 757 corrects this?

options.text: An instruction to prioritize speed over every posture
The repeated instruction to become composed in the prayer's postures
A rule that only the opening words matter
A claim that movements need no attention

questions.explanation: The Prophet's correction of the man's prayer includes deliberate settling in its principal postures.

questions.question: A person continues shopping when the Friday prayer call addressed in Quran 62:9 is made. What does the verse tell those addressed to do?

options.text: Treat business as a substitute for the gathering.
Wait until the next day before responding.
Leave trade and proceed to Allah's remembrance.
Assume the instruction concerns only sellers, never buyers.

questions.explanation: The verse prioritizes the Friday gathering over trade at the specified call. This question does not define every condition of personal obligation.

questions.question: Someone who is fasting eats or drinks out of genuine forgetfulness. What does Sahih al-Bukhari 1933 tell them to do?

options.text: End the fast for the rest of the day.
Treat the mistake as deliberate rejection of fasting.
Assume all future fasts are invalid.
Continue the fast.

questions.explanation: The narration specifically addresses forgetful eating or drinking and instructs completing the fast.

questions.question: A fasting person avoids food but continues deliberate lying. What warning in Sahih al-Bukhari 1903 is relevant?

options.text: Fasting must not be separated from abandoning false speech and conduct.
Avoiding food makes lying harmless.
The report encourages lying when hungry.
The report says all truthful speech breaks the fast.

questions.explanation: The narration strongly rebukes false speech and acting on it while fasting. It should not be misused as a command to start eating.

questions.question: Someone tries to provoke a fasting person into a fight. What response is taught in Sahih al-Bukhari 1894?

options.text: Assume hunger permits verbal abuse.
Avoid abusive conduct and identify oneself as fasting.
Escalate the dispute to prove resolve.
Break the fast to win the argument.

questions.explanation: The narration describes fasting as a shield and teaches restraint in response to provocation.

questions.question: What does Quran 2:185 provide for a person who is ill or travelling and does not fast under the concession?

options.text: Treat every missed day as permanently unaccountable.
Replace all future Ramadans with one donation automatically.
Make up the missed days on other days.
Assume the concession means Ramadan fasting was never prescribed.

questions.explanation: The verse states an equivalent number of other days and emphasizes Allah's desire for ease. Individual eligibility requires attention to the actual circumstances.

questions.question: According to Aishah's report in Sahih Muslim 335c, what was the instruction after menstruation regarding missed worship?

options.text: Make up the prayers, but not the fasts.
Make up neither prayers nor fasts.
Make up every prayer twice.
Make up the fasts, but not the prayers.

questions.explanation: Aishah distinguishes the instruction concerning missed fasts from that concerning missed prayers.

questions.question: A donor repeatedly humiliates a recipient by mentioning their help. Which warning in Quran 2:264 applies?

options.text: Do not spoil charity through reminders of favours and hurt.
Donating creates a right to humiliate.
Financial help makes respectful speech unnecessary.
Recipients must praise a donor publicly for charity to count.

questions.explanation: The verse links the manner of giving with the protection of the charitable deed.

questions.question: A person stops making dua because the requested outcome has not appeared quickly. What does Sahih al-Bukhari 6340 warn against?

options.text: Asking Allah sincerely more than once
Impatience expressed by saying one prayed but was not answered
Admitting one's dependence on Allah
Seeking good for another person

questions.explanation: The narration cautions against impatiently giving up; it does not promise the requested outcome on a personal deadline.

questions.question: Someone pursues voluntary worship while neglecting their body and family. What lesson does Sahih al-Bukhari 1968 provide?

options.text: Voluntary worship removes every family responsibility.
Physical needs always have no relevance to worship.
Give Allah, oneself and one's family their respective rights.
Neglect proves superior devotion by itself.

questions.explanation: The Prophet approved Salman's counsel to Abu al-Darda about recognizing and fulfilling these rights.

questions.question: A person wants more voluntary practices but regularly neglects obligatory duties. Which principle in Sahih al-Bukhari 6502 should guide priorities?

options.text: Voluntary acts always cancel every neglected duty.
A long optional routine makes obligations irrelevant.
Religious priorities depend only on personal enjoyment.
The obligatory duties are foremost among acts by which a servant draws near to Allah.

questions.explanation: The narration places what Allah has made obligatory before continued approach through voluntary deeds.

questions.question: According to Quran 2:271, which assessment of giving openly or secretly is most accurate?

options.text: Open charity can be good, while discreet giving to the poor is described as better.
Every publicly visible donation is automatically invalid.
Secret giving is forbidden.
Only the size of an audience determines a gift's value.

questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes praise of giving from the added value of concealing a gift to the poor.

questions.question: Quran 5:6 concludes its purification instructions by rejecting an intention to impose hardship. What is the most careful inference?

options.text: Any inconvenience automatically cancels every purification rule.
Prescribed purification and lawful accommodations belong together; ease does not mean inventing personal exemptions.
Tayammum proves that ordinary wudu has no purpose.
The verse requires hardship as an end in itself.

questions.explanation: The conclusion explains purification and Allah's favour while the verse itself retains instructions and conditions.

questions.question: A person uses Sahih al-Bukhari 137 to claim that wudu remains valid even when they are certain they passed wind silently. What has been confused?

options.text: The report prohibits all prayer after wudu.
The report makes every smell invalidate everyone's wudu.
An instruction about mere doubt has been turned into permission to ignore a certain event.
The report concerns only the cleanliness of clothing.

questions.explanation: The report addresses uncertainty. Sound and smell are not permissions to dismiss an event known with certainty; Sahih al-Bukhari 135 separately requires ablution after an invalidating event.

questions.question: A learner reads the advice about three monthly fasts and concludes that these replace Ramadan. Which distinction resolves the mistake?

options.text: The three monthly fasts were the only fasts ever taught.
Ramadan is merely a name for any three days.
A companion's advice cancels a Quranic obligation automatically.
A recommended monthly practice does not replace the separately prescribed Ramadan fast.

questions.explanation: Read the advice in Sahih al-Bukhari 1981 alongside the Ramadan instruction in Quran 2:185, rather than making one erase the other.

questions.question: An app says it is iftar time using a city in another time zone, but the sun has not set at the user's location. Which principle should govern?

options.text: The relevant local sunset must be established; a mismatched app setting is not the fasting boundary.
Any notification makes eating permissible everywhere.
The phone's display overrides the physical timing described in the narration.
Every place on Earth shares one sunset time.

questions.explanation: The narration's sunset criterion must be applied to the relevant location. Technology assists timing rather than creating the worship boundary.

questions.question: A person assumes they may keep eating until sunrise because dawn and sunrise are the same event. Which distinction matters in Quran 2:187?

options.text: The verse explicitly sets the boundary at midday.
The fasting boundary is dawn, which occurs before sunrise.
Sunrise is always earlier than dawn.
The verse has no starting boundary for fasting.

questions.explanation: The verse uses the distinction of dawn, not the later appearance of the sun, as the beginning of the abstention period.

questions.question: Someone claims the warnings about false speech while fasting prove that lying automatically requires ending the fast with food. What is the sounder conclusion?

options.text: The warning makes deliberate lying a recommended way to end fasting.
The warning replaces every fasting rule with a speech rule.
The warning demands abandoning sinful conduct; it is not an instruction to eat.
The warning says food and drink are irrelevant to fasting.

questions.explanation: The report's severe moral warning should not be converted into an unstated command to break the fast.

questions.question: Someone wants to fast on Eid al-Fitr because they feel unusually sincere that day. What principle follows from Sahih al-Bukhari 1990?

options.text: Sincerity changes the day into an ordinary voluntary fasting day.
The prohibition applies only when no one feels motivated.
The report prohibits Eid prayer rather than fasting.
A sincere personal wish does not remove the prohibition on fasting that day.

questions.explanation: Worship includes respecting the specified limits, rather than treating enthusiasm as permission to reverse them.

questions.question: A person assumes any useful donation automatically fulfils their zakat. Which issue raised by Quran 9:60 must first be examined?

options.text: Whether it reaches an eligible recipient category, alongside the other applicable zakat conditions
Only whether the donor liked the project
Only whether the payment was made through an app
Whether the recipient promised social-media promotion

questions.explanation: The verse specifies recipients for obligatory charity. A useful gift and valid payment of zakat are not automatically identical.

questions.question: Why should the illness accommodation in Sahih al-Bukhari 1117 not be interpreted as making every prayer posture optional for anyone?

options.text: It forbids prayer for everyone who is ill.
The instruction ties changes in posture to inability.
It says personal preference alone determines every posture.
It removes standing from every prayer permanently.

questions.explanation: The sequence of standing, sitting and lying on one's side is expressly linked to what the worshipper can do.

questions.question: Read together, how do Quran 62:9–10 frame worship and lawful livelihood?

options.text: Abandon all earning permanently after attending one Friday prayer.
Continue trade through the addressed call and postpone prayer indefinitely.
Leave trade for the addressed Friday gathering, then lawful activity may resume after prayer with remembrance of Allah.
Treat earning and remembering Allah as impossible to combine.

questions.explanation: The two verses give a time-specific priority and then permit dispersing to seek Allah's bounty, while retaining remembrance.

questions.question: Someone reads Quran 7:55 as proof that Allah cannot hear a quiet supplication. What does the verse actually support?

options.text: Dua is heard only if shouted.
Private supplication has no place in worship.
Allah requires an audience to know a person's needs.
Calling on Allah humbly and quietly is meaningful worship.

questions.explanation: The command to call privately or discreetly contradicts the assumption that quietness prevents supplication from reaching Allah.

questions.question: A person cites Quran 3:191 to say remembrance while lying down removes the need for obligatory prayer. What distinction is needed?

options.text: The availability of remembrance in different postures does not cancel the separate obligation of prayer.
The verse says lying down is always the only valid prayer posture.
The verse abolishes prescribed prayer times.
Only people who cannot remember Allah need prayer.

questions.explanation: Read the description of remembrance alongside Quran 4:103's statement of prayer as a timed obligation.

questions.question: A donor hides the amount of a gift but privately humiliates its recipient. Which assessment best combines Quran 2:271 and 2:264?

options.text: Privacy automatically makes every manner of giving acceptable.
Concealment does not excuse reminders of favours or hurtful treatment.
Only public insults can harm charity.
Concealing a gift removes the recipient's dignity.

questions.explanation: The praise of discreet giving should be read with the prohibition on spoiling charity through hurt.

questions.question: Does the report of intensified worship in the last ten nights establish that worship in the rest of Ramadan is unnecessary?

options.text: Yes; no worship matters before the final ten nights.
Yes; all earlier obligatory prayers become optional.
No; it describes increased dedication, not cancellation of worship at other times.
No; the report actually forbids extra worship in the last ten nights.

questions.explanation: A report about increased effort in a special period should not be made to abolish duties or devotion outside it.

questions.question: Someone cites the encouragement of voluntary worship but ignores obligations to dependants. Which pairing best corrects their priorities?

options.text: Increase voluntary acts until dependants no longer need support.
Treat family duties as obstacles without religious significance.
Assume greater exhaustion always means greater obedience.
Fulfil obligatory duties and give the family its due while maintaining voluntary devotion.

questions.explanation: The report on obligations and the approved counsel about personal and family rights should inform a sustainable worship routine together.
